newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden to probe Nazi gold allegations.
newsitem.headline: Sweden to probe Nazi gold allegations.

text.p: Sweden said on Friday it would launch a formal investigation of allegations by the World Jewish Congress (WJC) that Nazi gold from World War Two had found its way into official Swedish bank vaults.

The Riksbank, the country's central bank, said in a statement: "We have found there is reason to carry out a fresh investigation of the bank's archives to discover if any light can be shed on the Riksbank's acquisition of so-called stolen gold."
The Riksbank said the WJC had called for details about such gold in neutral states like Switzerland and Sweden to be made public.
"The Riksbank wishes to obtain as clear a picture as possible of the circumstances under which the bank acquired gold from Nazi Germany," it said.
The Riksbank governor would appoint three people who have no connection to the central bank to conduct the investigation, which is due to be completed in the first half of 1997.
Sweden's Riksbank has already returned over 13 tonnes of gold to Belgium and The Netherlands which was presumed to have been looted following an investigation carried out after World War Two.
